question: Does camera identity alone carry enough target-label information to become a plausible shortcut in a future Artemis II image task?
terminal_objective: Test acquisition-device confounding as an independent consequence of the task-conditioned sample hierarchy, without training a pixel model or declaring the archive labels correct.
method: Use one source-representation row per admitted exposure, exclude blank target labels, freeze the Data User Guide's independent operational statement that the Z9 was the primary eclipse camera, measure the complete target-by-camera contingency, and score the deliberately simple diagnostic rule 'predict Sunset iff Z9'.
authority: Private local metadata and document analysis only. No pixels, model training, publication, target-label validation, causal claim, held-out prediction claim, shortcut-use claim, actual leakage claim, performance-effect claim, scientific-discovery claim, or cross-mission generalization.
claim_ceiling: Stage 10U may establish a descriptive acquisition-device/target-label association in the verified complete-action cohort: among 3,413 source exposures with nonblank target labels, 19 of 23 target classes occur on one camera only and account for 807 exposures; 593 of 734 labeled Z9 exposures carry Sunset. The document-nominated rule 'predict Sunset iff Z9' scores 67.741% accuracy versus a 54.498% majority baseline, 65.302% balanced accuracy, 80.790% precision, and 38.184% sensitivity. Sunset itself spans two cameras, so camera identity is neither necessary nor sufficient. The result cannot establish target-label correctness, causation, pixel-encoded camera identity, actual model shortcut use, leakage, a held-out performance gain, archive-wide or cross-mission prevalence, scientific discovery, novelty, or priority.

next_step_logic.if_target_classification_is_selected: Require a camera-only metadata baseline and camera/event-stratified evaluation before interpreting pixel-model performance; report unsupported camera-target cells rather than hiding them in a random split.
next_step_logic.if_pixels_are_used: Test camera identifiability and target performance under camera-held-out or balanced conditions separately; do not infer a pixel shortcut from metadata association alone.
next_step_logic.if_new_event_generalization_is_selected: The Stage 10T single-event limit still controls; camera balancing cannot manufacture a second Sunset event.
next_step_logic.if_no_target_model_is_selected: Preserve this as a prospective confounding canary and do not train a model merely to make the hazard concrete.
next_step_logic.recheck_trigger: A real target-classification task, validated target labels, additional comparable events, or a public Artemis II image model.
